# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** Dean Health Plan — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Quinn Grant
Member ID: W331641494
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-10 — Reference number POC-5BC8A5312C-11722**
**Requested service:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Denial reason given:** the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery
**Governing policy:** Carelon Spine Surgery — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Dean Health Plan's denial of the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested for me by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, an orthopedic surgeon, who has documented that this surgery is medically necessary for me. The denial notice states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking for reconsideration because the plan's own published criteria, quoted below, describe the exact care I completed, and my records document it.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the notice; the appeal must be received by **2027-02-06**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. (Members can also call the number on the back of the insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.)

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. What counts as conservative management**

The Carelon Spine Surgery policy states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records document both parts of this requirement:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, 16 weeks, from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary treatment strategies (more than one):** NSAIDs for 4 months, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21.

**2. Failure of conservative management**

The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

Mapping my records to each part:

- **Completed a full course for the current episode of care:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24), 4 months of NSAIDs, and an injection on 2026-04-21.
- **Worsening of or no significant improvement:** my symptoms are described in the records as 24 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief. The corticosteroid injection gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **More invasive forms of therapy are being considered:** the ACDF at issue in this appeal is exactly that, and it is the reason the prior authorization was submitted.

**3. The policy's own stated duration for conservative management**

Where the policy states a time period for conservative care, it states:

> "Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

and

> "Radicular pain (with or without demonstrable neurologic deficits) which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of conservative management Documentation of a synovial cyst on CT or MRI performed within the past 6 months which correlates with symptoms and exam findings"

My documented physical therapy alone ran 16 weeks, which is more than twice the 6 weeks the policy names, and it was combined with 4 months of NSAIDs and an injection. I am not aware of any longer duration stated in the policy language I have; if Dean Health Plan applied a longer or different requirement, I am asking that it be identified in writing in the appeal response.

**4. Imaging correlating with my symptoms and exam**

The policy states:

> "When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:"

My MRI of the cervical spine on 2026-07-13 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. My symptoms match that level: radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness. My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The policy also states:

> "Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement"

That is what my chart documents.

The policy further states:

> "Imaging studies – All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My MRI findings and my clinical findings point to the same level and the same nerve. If the plan needs the radiologist's report itself, I will provide it on request: [name of imaging facility / radiologist report for the 2026-07-13 MRI].

**5. Surgical risk factors the policy asks about**

The policy states:

> "Tobacco cessation – Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis."

My records document that I am a non-smoker. They also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## A note about the criteria I was given

Two of the passages in the plan's policy end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me — including the passage that begins:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

I am not attempting to guess at the contents of those lists. If Dean Health Plan relied on any item within them, I am asking the plan to identify in its appeal response the specific criterion it applied and the specific part of my record it found lacking, so that I can respond to it directly. Everything I have argued above is tied to policy language I have quoted word for word; I have not quoted or characterized any policy text I was not given.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Dean Health Plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-10 (reference POC-5BC8A5312C-11722) and authorize the cervical fusion (CPT 22551) requested by Dr. Marchetti. Specifically, I ask that the reviewer:

1. Re-review my physical therapy discharge note (16 visits, 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24), my medication history, the 2026-04-21 injection record, and the 2026-07-13 MRI report;
2. Consider those records against the conservative-management language quoted above; and
3. If the denial is maintained, provide a written explanation that names the specific criterion applied and the specific documentation the plan considers missing, along with the qualifications of the reviewer who made the decision and information about my further appeal rights, including external review.

I am glad to provide any additional records the plan needs. Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address], and my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone number].

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Grant**
Member ID: W331641494
Date of birth: [my date of birth]
Reference number: POC-5BC8A5312C-11722
Signature: ______________________ Date: ____________

**Enclosures (to attach):**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-10
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, 16 visits)
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-21
- MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-07-13
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, including exam findings
- [Any other records my surgeon's office recommends including]

quotes: Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:

Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy.

Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered

For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs.

Imaging studies – All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure.

Symptomatic, non-traumatic cervical spondylosis as demonstrated by EITHER of the following radiographic findings: Sagittal plane angulation of greater than 11 degrees between adjacent segments Subluxation or translation of greater than 3 mm on static lateral views or dynamic radiographs

When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:
Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)
Imaging studies which demonstrate cervical cord compression

Radicular pain (with or without demonstrable neurologic deficits) which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of conservative management Documentation of a synovial cyst on CT or MRI performed within the past 6 months which correlates with symptoms and exam findings

Advanced imaging studies highly suggestive of nonunion at a motion segment at which a fusion had been previously attempted. This includes lack of bridging bone and/or dynamic motion demonstrated on flexion-extension radiographs

Tobacco cessation – Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis.

The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present.
Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement
Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to spinal cord or foraminal compression

Clinical signs and symptoms of myelopathy which may include loss of dexterity, urinary urgency, new-onset bowel or bladder incontinence, frequent falls, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, increased tone or spasticity, gait abnormality, or pathologic Babinski sign
